definition: Degenerate means to sink into a worse or lower state — to lose the quality or character that made something what it was.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word degenerate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know degenerate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Without its moderator the neighborhood forum degenerated in a single winter, careful book threads giving way to feuds and spam.

Worsen is weaker than degenerate: a worsening debate grows testier but is still a debate, while a degenerating one is sliding into something lower — a shouting match that has stopped being debate at all.

Disintegrate goes further than degenerate: a degenerated league has sunk into a worse version of itself, but a league that disintegrates comes apart completely, leaving nothing whole enough to have a character at all.

Decay is physical rot — teeth, timber, fallen fruit breaking down into ruin. Degenerate is broader and aims at character: a debate, a league, or a friendship degenerates when it slides into a lower version of itself, no rot required.

Regress means to slip back to an earlier stage: a patient regresses, a skill regresses under stress. It measures backward motion and says nothing about quality. Degenerate adds the fall: what comes out the far end is not just earlier but worse.

Its unit-mate deteriorate covers the field's fate that same summer: weeds, a sagging backstop, a condition running down while the field stayed a field.

The best years produced minor legends — a rowboat on a roof, a statue in a borrowed scarf, four hundred forks planted on a lawn.
